title: Seven Winters and One Short Note
subtitle: 人际交往 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际交往（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通）
meta: 主题语境：人际交往（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通）　|　核心词汇：favour　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 favour 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 my grandmother ① asked a favour that no neighbour in the lane would have returned, and she said the asking was the whole of the winter. The ② favour, meaning the help itself and not the gift, ran seven winters and stayed unreturned in the book; a favour, she said, is the only thing in a lane that is judged by how long it is left unreturned.

Every ③ favour in that lane had the same short note beside it, and the ④ favour at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A favour, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to return; my grandmother said the returning is the part that fills seven winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the favour was the whole of the matter, meaning the approval and not the help. The ⑥ favour, meaning the approval and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody returns; favour, he said, is either something you ask or the only word that means both help and approval. He said the approval is the part they remember.

By 1955 the ⑦ favour had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short note. The ⑧ favour of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one lane and seven winters of returning; favour, she said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to return. She said the returning was never mentioned.

The ⑨ favour I remember is the one returned in the letter, which closed in 1957 and is still described as the quietest in the lane. A ⑩ favour, my mother said in 1959, is the only one that improves by being returned; every favour, she said, is approval that has agreed to look like help. She said the approval was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 恩惠；帮忙（指巷子里每一次旁边的那一次）
B. n. 帮忙（指那一次本身，与礼物相对）
C. 固定搭配：ask a favour 请人帮一个忙
D. n. 帮忙（指留给孩子的那一次）
E. n. 恩惠（抽象总称，指一条巷子的人情之事）
F. n. 恩惠（指信上写到、被回报的那一次）
G. n. 赞成；支持（指一件事里人人都等却无人回报的那样东西）
H. n. 支持（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人回报的那样东西）

answers.why: ask a favour 意为“请人帮一个忙”，1948 年祖母请了一个巷子里没有一位邻居肯回报的忙。
favour 意为“帮忙”，指那一次本身而不是礼物，它经过了七个冬天而在簿子上没有记号。
favour 意为“恩惠、帮忙”，指巷子里每一次旁边的那一次，每一次旁边都有同一张短短的字条。
favour 意为“帮忙”，指留给孩子的那一次，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
favour 意为“赞成、支持”，指一件事里人人都等却无人回报的那样东西，叔叔说这份支持就是那件事的全部。
favour 意为“支持”，指人人都等却无人回报的那样东西而不是那一次帮忙，是事情里人人都等、却无人回报的东西。
favour 意为“恩惠”，指信上写到、被回报的那一次，到 1955 年这一次成了信里的一行。
favour 意为“恩惠”，祖母一月写道，整件事的人情之事是一条巷子和七个冬天的回报。
favour 意为“恩惠”，我记得的是信上回报的那一次，1957 年结束了，至今仍被说成巷子里最安静的一次。
favour 为抽象总称，母亲 1959 年说，一次帮忙是唯一会因为被好好回报而变得更好的东西。
